My request stands as a student here: that the readers around campus be removed and that no new ones be installed. The ownership terms would at least tell us what kind of deal this is. Could you find out and reply? I would be grateful.

subject: Writing ahead of the budget hearing on this
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Writing ahead of the next budget discussion so my point is not a surprise. The recurring cost of automated license plate readers around {{school}} seems to me to deserve a line of its own and a vote of its own, and I plan to say so publicly.

If you would like the argument in advance, it is short. Money committed indefinitely without a stated figure is money outside democratic control, and the {{role}} could fix that in an afternoon.

The outcome I hope for, as one student, is removal of the readers near campus and a commitment that {{city}} will install no more. Between now and the hearing, could you tell me what the program costs and whether you would support ending it? I would rather understand your view before I speak than after.

subject: The longer we wait, the harder removal becomes
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Deployments are easier to prevent than to undo. Once mounts are in and workflows adapt, removal takes on its own price tag, and that price grows every year the question is put off. That is what makes me want to raise it now rather than later.

So I am asking now, as a student here. Remove the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} and install no new ones, before reversing course costs more than it does today.

I recognize this is not the only consideration in front of you, and I would not pretend otherwise. Even so, the fiscal logic seems to point one way, and residents of {{city}} have not been given a competing figure to weigh against it. Would you tell me what you think the program costs and whether you could vote to end it?

subject: Was any cost-benefit work done before signing
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Standard practice for a recurring commitment is some form of cost-benefit work before the signature, however rough. Residents of {{city}} cannot tell whether that happened for the plate reader program, because nothing of the kind appears in the public record, and the silence is what unsettles me.

Did the {{role}} receive an analysis? If a vendor produced it, was it checked by anyone without a stake in the outcome?

My request, as a student here, is that the readers around {{school}} be removed and that none be installed after them. An independent analysis might change my mind, and I would read one seriously and say so. Without it, the recurring payments look to me more like a habit than a decision. Could you tell me what analysis exists?

subject: Future upgrade charges already built into the deal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Equipment gets superseded, and vendors have every reason to supersede it. If the plate reader agreement covering {{city}} contemplates hardware refreshes, then the cost the {{role}} approved once will return later in a larger form. That prospect is what prompts this letter.

Could you find out whether upgrade or refresh charges are part of the arrangement, and whether they need a new appropriation or fall under the existing one?

My own answer to the upgrade question is that there should be nothing left to upgrade. I am a student here, and I would like the readers near {{school}} taken down with no new ones installed. Short of that, residents deserve to know what future charges are already baked into a contract signed on their behalf. Would you look into it and reply?

subject: What share of the department budget goes to cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

One thing residents cannot currently work out is how much of the department's budget in {{city}} goes to camera systems rather than to people. That proportion is a policy choice, and it appears to be getting made without any public discussion, which is the part I find hard to accept.

Would you ask for the breakdown and make it available? A single page would do.

My position, as a student here, is that automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} should be removed and that none should be installed to replace them. The breakdown matters because it would show what else the same money supports, and because I do not think the {{role}} can weigh a tradeoff it has never seen written down. Would you request the figures and tell me your view?

subject: Approved once, and billed again every year
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The structural problem with the plate reader spending in {{city}} fits in a sentence. A decision taken once produces a bill that arrives every year, and nothing in the process makes anyone look at it again. That is what I would most like to see change.

It seems to me reason enough for the {{role}} to look now, with the amount stated and the funding source named.

When it does, I hope the outcome is removal of the readers around {{school}} and a commitment to install no more. I am one student and you may prefer a different outcome, which is fair, so long as the decision is actually taken rather than inherited. Would you put the question before the body, and would you tell me how you would vote?

subject: Advance notice would let residents weigh in
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Residents cannot weigh in on a decision they hear about afterward. A simple rule would help: publish the terms of any surveillance contract renewal a reasonable time before the {{role}} acts on it.

Applied to the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}, that means the cost and the cancellation provisions, posted somewhere residents can find them.

What I would do with that information, as a student here, is argue for taking the readers down and installing no new ones in {{city}}. Others would argue the opposite, and they should have the same chance. Advance notice is what makes the argument possible at all, and its absence is why I am writing. Would you support the rule, and would you tell me your own position on the cameras? Thank you for reading.

subject: The city may not control what renewal costs
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A budget line a vendor can move is not really under local control. Unless the agreement caps increases, the price {{city}} pays for automated license plate readers at the next renewal gets decided somewhere other than the {{role}} chamber. That is the part that worries me most about the arrangement.

Is there a cap? If not, would you consider declining to renew rather than accepting terms the city cannot influence?

The answer I am hoping for is broader than that. I am a student here, and I would like the readers near {{school}} removed with none installed afterward, which ends the exposure for good. Even a member who supports the technology might be uneasy about an open-ended price. Where do you come out on it?

subject: What else is bundled into the reader contract
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Vendors like to bundle. A contract that appears to cover cameras may also include software and access to systems residents have never heard discussed at a public meeting, all under one recurring figure. That is difficult to evaluate from outside, and it is why I am asking rather than asserting.

What exactly does the {{city}} agreement cover beyond the readers themselves near {{school}}? Bundling makes spending harder to judge and easier to renew, which is presumably part of its appeal to the seller.

I would like the {{role}} to unbundle the question and then answer it by removing the readers around campus and approving no new installations. I am a student here, and if you disagree with me, an itemized description would at least let residents disagree with you on the facts. Would you obtain one?

subject: Asking simply where you stand on continued funding
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

No argument in this one, just a request for a position. As {{officialTitle}}, would you vote to continue funding automated license plate readers in {{city}}, or would you vote to stop?

I ask because constituents deserve to know how their representatives intend to handle recurring spending before it renews, especially spending that has never been debated in public with a figure attached.

For my part, I am a student here and I would like the readers near {{shortName}} removed with no new ones installed. You may hold the opposite view, and I would rather hear it than not. A clear statement either way would be more useful to me than a summary of the program's purpose, which I have already read. Could you give me one? Thank you for your time.

subject: Does the city keep a register of recurring contracts
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Many organizations have learned the hard way to keep a register of recurring contracts and review them on a schedule. Whether {{city}} does this, and whether the plate reader agreement sits on that register, would tell residents how seriously the recurring spending is managed.

Could you find out? If no register exists, the {{role}} might consider creating one, which would surface a good deal more than this single program.

The program itself I would like ended, with the readers around {{school}} removed and none installed in their place. I am one student and I may be missing something, though better contract management would probably reach a similar conclusion on its own. Would you support the register, and would you support the removal? I would be glad of an answer to either.

subject: Poles outlast the officials who approved them
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Poles and mounts outlast the officials who approve them. So does the contract that keeps the cameras on them running, which is how one evening's agenda item becomes a permanent feature of the budget in {{city}}. That permanence is what I find difficult.

I would like the {{role}} to treat the plate readers around {{shortName}} as the long-term commitment they appear to be, and to decide accordingly.

Deciding accordingly, in my view as a student here, means removing them and installing no new ones. If the body decides otherwise, I hope it will at least do so knowing the lifetime cost rather than the annual one. Has anyone calculated that? If not, would you ask for it? I would be grateful either way, and thank you for reading.

subject: What comparable cities pay for the same service
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Benchmarking is ordinary procurement practice. Before renewing, it seems reasonable for {{city}} to find out what comparable jurisdictions pay for the same service and whether their terms differ.

Has anyone done that work? If the price here is higher than elsewhere, the {{role}} has leverage it does not appear to be using. If it is lower, saying so publicly costs nothing.

My preference is that the comparison becomes irrelevant because the automated license plate readers around {{school}} are removed and none are installed to replace them. That is what I am asking for as a student here. Short of it, benchmarking would give residents some way to judge whether the recurring cost is defensible, which we presently lack. Would you request it, and would you share what comes back?

subject: Did the promised savings ever appear
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

New systems are often sold partly on the savings they will produce. If anything of that kind was claimed when the plate readers near {{shortName}} were approved, the natural follow-up is whether the savings appeared and where they show up in the accounts of {{city}}.

Could you ask? A program that promised savings and produced none seems to me an easy candidate for the list of things the {{role}} stops funding.

Stopping is what I would like, as a student here, with the readers around campus removed and no new ones installed. The savings question is one route there, and it is a question the body can answer from its own records. Would you raise it, and what do you expect the answer will be? I would be grateful to hear.

subject: Is this the best use of recurring public money
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Stripped of everything else, the question is simple. Is an indefinite subscription for automated license plate readers the best available use of that money in {{city}}?

I do not think it is, though I hold that view with less certainty than I would like. Residents cannot check my reasoning against yours, because the amount has never been published anywhere findable, which itself suggests the question has not been examined closely.

I would like the {{role}} to examine it, and to conclude by removing the readers around {{school}} and approving no new ones. If the body concludes otherwise, it will at least have taken a decision rather than inherited one. As one student, that is most of what I am asking for. Would you tell me how you would answer the question?

subject: Pulling this item out of the omnibus vote
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Items buried in a large budget package get approved without ever being considered on their own. That is convenient for administration and poor for accountability, and it describes how surveillance spending usually passes.

Would you move to separate the automated license plate reader funding from the omnibus vote, so the {{role}} takes a distinct decision on it with the recurring cost stated?

On the merits, I am a student who would like the readers near {{school}} removed and no new ones installed in {{city}}. A separate vote is how residents find out who agrees with them. Whether or not you share my position, would you support pulling the item out for its own consideration? I would be grateful for a reply, and grateful still if the answer is no but comes with a reason.

subject: No certainty about what this will cost later
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

One thing a public body should want from a contract is knowing what it will pay. Open-ended service agreements offer the opposite, particularly where the vendor sets renewal pricing and the buyer has grown used to the tool.

Does {{city}} have cost certainty on the plate readers around {{shortName}} for the remaining term and beyond it? It seems to me the {{role}} would want that answer before committing again, and I cannot find it myself.

My request does not depend on the answer. I am a student here, and I would like the readers near campus removed with none installed in their place, which makes cost certainty easy to achieve. Would you find out what the future pricing looks like, and tell me whether you would vote to accept it? Thank you for considering this.

subject: Is this justified by safety or by revenue
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Systems like this are sometimes defended as a public safety measure and sometimes as a revenue-producing one, and the two justifications call for quite different scrutiny. Residents of {{city}} have not been told which applies here, and I would like to know before forming a firmer view.

If the plate readers near {{school}} are expected to produce revenue, I would like that expectation stated openly, along with what happens to the program if the revenue does not appear. Without such an expectation, the recurring cost stands entirely on its own.

Either way, I am a student asking for removal of the readers around campus and no new installations. I hope the {{role}} can say plainly what the money is for. Could you tell me which justification you rely on?

subject: Every month of delay is another month of payments
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Deferral has a price here that it does not have elsewhere. Every month the {{role}} does not take up the plate reader question, {{city}} pays for another month of service, and the case for continuity grows a little stronger through nothing but elapsed time. That is what makes me want to write now rather than wait.

It seems to me a reason to schedule the discussion soon rather than at the next convenient moment.

When it happens, I hope the decision is removal of the readers around {{shortName}} and a commitment to install none in future. I am one student, and if the body decides differently, at least the money will have been spent deliberately. Would you push for the item to be scheduled, and could you tell me how you would vote?

subject: The money side of this, set out briefly
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Setting privacy aside for a moment, the money side troubles me on its own. The cost recurs, the total has not been published, the renewal happens without a vote, and nobody has shown what the spending buys.

Any one of those would justify a review by the {{role}}. Together they are why I am asking for the program to end: remove the automated license plate readers around {{school}}, and install no new ones in {{city}}.

I would much rather be argued out of this position with figures than left with silence. I am a student here, and if the accounts support the program, publishing them would be the simplest way to answer letters like mine. Would you publish them, or would you support removal? Either reply would be welcome, and thank you for reading.

subject: A standing commitment against spending on more readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Whatever happens to the existing contract, the {{role}} could decide today not to spend more. A standing commitment against funding additional automated license plate readers in {{city}} would cost nothing to make and would settle a recurring question before it arrives.

Alongside it, I am asking that the readers already in place around {{shortName}} be removed. Mapped data counts {{readersWithinMile}} of them within a mile of campus, each attached to a payment that continues indefinitely.

Residents cannot audit what they cannot see, and at present the cost of this program is not visible in anything the city publishes. As a student here, that is the part that stays with me. Would you make the commitment, and would you tell me where you stand on removal? Thank you for taking the time to read this.

subject: Asking about the plate readers near {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} taken down, and I am hoping the city will not approve any more of them.

I study at {{school}} and am on or near campus most days. Having my car photographed and logged every time it passes is not something I ever agreed to, and it sits badly with me. The cameras keep running whether or not anyone nearby has done anything wrong.

Knowing where you stand before the next contract comes up would help me a great deal. Even a short reply would be welcome. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: {{readersWithinMile}} plate readers sit within a mile of campus
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

There are {{readersWithinMile}} automated license plate readers within a mile of {{school}}, where I am a student. That figure is most of what worries me. I would like every one of them removed, with nothing installed to replace them.

Having my car photographed and filed because I drove to class is not something I want. The cameras cannot tell the difference between somebody worth watching and everybody else, and a permanent record of who was where feels like more than {{city}} needs.

You are in a position to change this, and I would be grateful to know whether you will.

subject: The case for cameras around {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

I have been looking for the argument in favor of keeping automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}, and I have not found one that accounts for photographing everyone who drives past.

That is why I am asking you to support taking them out, with no new ones installed near campus. I am a student at {{school}}, so this is the area I move through every day.

Surveillance that runs by default on people who have done nothing seems like the sort of thing a city should have to explain out loud. If there is an explanation I have missed, I would like to hear it.

subject: A vote that would remove the campus readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A vote on these cameras would settle something that has bothered me all year. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope the answer to any request for more is no.

I am a student there, and I never agreed to have my car logged each time I drive in. Neither did the people who live in {{city}} year round. Recording everybody in order to find somebody strikes me as a poor trade, however convenient it is.

Would you tell me how you expect to vote when this comes up? Thank you.

subject: I would rather not have plate readers at {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

I do not want automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}, I would like the ones already installed to come out, and I hope no new ones go in.

That is the whole of it. No theory about crime, no argument about government. I am a student at {{school}}, I walk and drive through the area constantly, and being recorded by default is what I object to. The cameras treat an ordinary trip to class the way they would treat a suspect, which seems backward to me.

Whatever your view turns out to be, I would rather hear it from you than guess. Would you write back and tell me?

subject: Concerns about the cameras around {{school}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

My concern is with the automated license plate readers around campus. I would like them taken down, and I hope {{city}} will not buy more.

I am a student at {{school}}. My car is photographed on the way in and again on the way out, and a record of that sits somewhere I cannot see, held by people I did not choose. Nothing about it was put to students, or to residents, before the cameras went up.

A program most people never agreed to seems like a reasonable one to end. Could you tell me where you stand on ending it?

subject: Reader counts near {{shortName}} and across {{state}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Between {{readersWithinMile}} automated license plate readers within a mile of {{shortName}} and {{readersInState}} of them across {{state}}, the scale of this is what unsettles me most.

I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the readers near campus removed, with no new ones approved. One camera is a tool. This many becomes a habit that nobody decided to form.

If the counts look different from where you sit, or if there is a reason for them I have not understood, I would genuinely like to hear it. A short reply would be plenty. Thank you.

subject: A short request about the campus plate readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

What I am asking for is short. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope the next proposal to add more is turned down.

Being a student here means passing those cameras several times a day. Each pass leaves a record I did not agree to and cannot look at. That is what bothers me, more than any particular use the readers might be put to.

I know one letter from one person is not much. Even so, I would be grateful to hear your position. Thank you for taking the time to read it.

subject: Two sentences about the readers near campus
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Two sentences will cover what I want. The automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} should come out, and I hope none go up in their place.

I am a student at {{school}}, writing once and for myself. What worries me is not any single camera but the habit of keeping a record of ordinary trips made by people who are not suspected of anything. That record outlasts whatever reason it was collected for.

If you disagree, I would still like to know. A line back with your position would be worth more to me than silence. Thank you.

subject: Would you vote to remove the campus readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Would you consider voting to take the automated license plate readers out of service around {{school}}? I am a student there, and that is the only thing I want from this letter, along with a decision against new ones.

The cameras photograph every car on the road, mine included, and keep what they see. Nobody asked whether that was a fair price for the area, and I do not think it is.

You may have heard arguments in favor that I have not. If so, I would like to hear them. Either way, I would appreciate a reply.

subject: Cars going past {{shortName}} are logged
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Cars going past {{shortName}} are logged by automated license plate readers, and I would rather my city did not do that. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the readers removed, with none installed later.

What sits with me is how ordinary the people being recorded are. Most of us are driving to class or to work. A record of that has to be stored, secured, and trusted to whoever holds it, and I have no way to check any of that.

Would you let me know your position? Even a brief note would help.

subject: If the plate reader contract comes back
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

If the automated license plate reader contract comes back for renewal, I am hoping you will vote against it, and I would like the cameras already installed around {{shortName}} taken down, with no new ones going in.

I am a student at {{school}}. Living beside cameras that read every plate feels different from living beside an officer who might notice one. The first sort never stops, never forgets, and never has to explain itself.

There may be a case for renewal that I have not seen. If there is, I would like to hear it from you. Thank you for reading this.

subject: Nothing I have read explains the readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Nothing I have read explains why automated license plate readers need to run on everybody. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the ones around campus taken out, with no new ones installed.

The part that stays with me is the default. If a camera watched only after some reason to look, I would feel differently. These start from the assumption that everyone's movements are worth keeping, and that assumption never gets argued for.

If you have heard a better case than I have, I would like to hear it. Otherwise I hope you will support removal. Thank you.

subject: Each reader near campus keeps a record
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Each of the readers around {{school}} keeps a record of people who are not suspected of anything, and mine is among them. I am a student there, and I would like the cameras removed and no more approved.

What worries me is not one photograph. It is the file that builds up behind it, held by somebody I cannot ask about it. Ordinary trips become a history that outlives whatever reason there was to collect it.

I would be grateful for your view, even if it differs from mine. A short reply would be enough to settle it. Thank you for reading.

subject: Before {{city}} approves another plate reader
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Before {{city}} approves another automated license plate reader, I would like to understand why the ones around {{school}} are there in the first place. I am a student on that campus and have not found an answer.

My hope is that the readers near campus come down and that no new ones are installed. The cameras run constantly on people going about a normal day, and that is the part I keep coming back to.

If there is a reason for them that would change my mind, I would honestly like to hear it. Thank you for your time.

subject: Is a review of the readers coming up
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Is there a review coming for the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}? If so, I would like them removed, and I hope any proposal for new ones is set aside.

I am a student at {{school}}, so the cameras sit on the roads I use most. Being photographed on an ordinary drive is not something I consented to, and there is no way for me to see what is kept or for how long.

Knowing your position would help me more than another round of searching. Would you write back, even briefly? Thank you.

subject: One decision from your office would help
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

One decision from your office would take the automated license plate readers around {{school}} out of service, and a second would keep new ones from going in. I am hoping for both.

I am a student here. The cameras photograph my car on trips that have nothing to do with anyone's investigation, and the record of that goes somewhere I cannot follow. That is the piece which unsettles me.

If either decision is further off than I think, I would still like to know where you stand. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: Nobody I know was asked about the cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Nobody I know was asked whether automated license plate readers should go up around {{shortName}}, and I include myself in that. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like them removed, with none added afterward.

The cameras keep working whether or not there is a reason to look at any particular car. That is a strange thing to have arrive without a public conversation, and it is what I keep thinking about.

I would be glad to hear your view on removal, even a short one. Thank you for taking the time.

subject: A student at {{shortName}} on the campus cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

As a student at {{school}}, I would like the automated license plate readers near campus removed, and I hope no new ones are installed. That is the request, and I will not dress it up.

What bothers me is the ordinariness of what gets recorded. Driving to class is not suspicious, and I would rather it were not logged and stored by default. Whoever holds those records is somebody I have no way to reach.

If you see a reason to keep them that I have overlooked, I would like to hear it. Otherwise I hope you will support taking them down.

subject: Two things I am hoping for from your office
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Two things would settle this for me. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} taken out of service, and I hope your office will stop approving new ones.

I am a student there, writing on my own behalf. The readers watch a road, not a suspect, and everyone who uses that road ends up in the record. That inversion is what I find hard to accept.

You may weigh this differently. If so, I would still rather hear your reasoning than assume it. A brief reply would be welcome. Thank you.

subject: About renewing the plate reader contract
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Renewing the automated license plate reader contract is something I am hoping to see declined, and I would like the cameras near {{shortName}} taken down rather than carried forward, with none added in their place.

I am a student at {{school}}. My objection is simple enough: the readers collect from everyone, all the time, and the people they collect from have no say in it and no view of it.

If renewal is already settled, I would still like to know your own position, and whether removal could be raised later. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: The cameras around {{shortName}} and what they collect
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Around {{shortName}} there are automated license plate readers that photograph every car going past, mine included. I would like them removed, and I hope your office will decline new ones.

I am a student at {{school}}, so I pass them often. What concerns me is that a record of ordinary movement is being kept about people who have not been accused of anything, and that the record is easier to keep than to delete.

Your view on this counts for more than mine does. Would you share it with me? A short answer either way would be appreciated.

subject: Counting the readers within a mile of {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Counting the automated license plate readers within a mile of {{shortName}} gives {{readersWithinMile}}. Every one of them points at people going about a normal day, and I would like all of them taken out with none installed later.

I am a student at {{school}}. The number is what got my attention, but the worry underneath it is simpler. Records of where people drove sit somewhere indefinitely, and nobody who is recorded gets a say.

I would be grateful for your position on removal. Even a line would help me understand where this stands. Thank you.

subject: Your position on the automated plate readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Your position on automated license plate readers is something I would like to know, because there are a number of them around {{school}}, where I am a student.

Mine is that they should be removed and that new ones should not be installed. The cameras photograph everybody who drives past and keep what they see, which is a lot of collecting for a problem I have never seen laid out.

If there is a reason for them that holds up, I would rather hear it than keep guessing. Would you reply and tell me how you see it? Thank you.

subject: Hoping for no more cameras around {{school}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

No more of these cameras is what I am hoping for, and I would like the automated license plate readers already around {{school}} removed as well.

I am a student here. The readers run without pause on roads that ordinary people use for ordinary reasons, and the record they build is not something anyone recorded can see or correct. That combination worries me more than the cameras themselves.

You hear from many people, I realize. Still, I would value a reply telling me whether removal is something you would support. Thank you for reading.

subject: The people these readers record are not suspects
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

People who have done nothing are the ones these readers spend their day recording, and I am one of them. I am a student at {{school}} who drives past the cameras near {{shortName}} most days.

I would like them removed, and I hope no new ones are approved. The trouble for me is that the collecting starts before there is any reason for it, and carries on afterward.

If you would tell me where you stand, I would appreciate it. A short answer is more than I have now. Thank you.

subject: Ending the plate reader program around campus
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Ending the automated license plate reader program would take one decision, and I am asking you to make it. The cameras near {{shortName}} should come down, and I hope nothing goes up to replace them.

I am a student at {{school}}, and I pass those readers on the way to class. Each pass adds to a record kept about somebody who is not under suspicion, which describes most of the people on that road.

Would you let me know whether removal is something you could support? I would be grateful for an answer either way.

subject: What keeping the campus cameras costs us
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Letting the readers stay feels to me like accepting a habit that nobody chose deliberately. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope none are installed in their place.

I am a student there. What worries me is how little it takes to keep a system like this running compared with how much it would take to unwind it later. The longer the records accumulate, the harder that gets.

If there is an argument for keeping them that I have not weighed properly, I would like to hear it. Thank you for your time.

subject: The short version of what worries me
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Here is the short version. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} taken down, and I hope {{city}} stops adding them.

I am a student at {{school}}, writing once rather than joining anything. Cameras that read every plate turn a normal drive into a record, and the person in the car has no part in the decision to keep it. That is the whole of my worry.

Your position would matter to me, whichever way it falls. Would you write back with it? Thank you for reading.

subject: About the next proposal for more readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The next proposal for more automated license plate readers is one I hope you will turn down, and I would like the ones already running around {{school}} taken out.

I am a student there, writing for myself. The cameras do not distinguish between a car worth looking at and the hundreds around it, so everybody ends up in the same file. I would rather my city did not keep that file at all.

If you would tell me how you are thinking about this, I would be grateful. A brief reply would be plenty. Thank you.

subject: My objection to the readers at {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Put simply, I am worried about the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}, and I would like them removed with no new ones installed. I am a student at {{school}}.

The cameras work continuously on people who have given no reason to be watched. Whatever is collected has to live somewhere, and I cannot find out where, for how long, or who can ask for it. That gap is most of what concerns me.

I would rather know your view than assume it. Would you reply and tell me where you stand? Thank you for the time.

subject: A ring of cameras was not what I expected
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Living inside a ring of automated license plate readers is not what I pictured when I enrolled at {{school}}. I would like the cameras around campus removed, and I hope no more are approved.

As a student here I drive the same few roads constantly, which means the same few cameras see me constantly. The record that builds from that is about a person who has done nothing, and it will outlast any reason for making it.

If you disagree, I would still like to hear why. A short reply would mean something. Thank you.

subject: Do the readers near {{shortName}} come up for review
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Do the automated license plate readers near {{shortName}} come up for review at some point? If they do, I am hoping they will be removed, and that proposals for new ones will be set aside.

I am a student at {{school}}. My worry is straightforward: the cameras collect from everyone who drives past, keep it, and give the people recorded no way to see or question what is held.

Even a short answer about timing and your own view would help. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: One request about the cameras at {{school}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

One request is all I have. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope no more are installed.

I am a student there. This is not something I want in the place where I spend most of my year, and nobody asked the people who live and study here about it. The cameras run all day on ordinary traffic, and the record does not go away when the day does.

Would you tell me whether you would support removal? I would be grateful for the answer. Thank you.

subject: {{state}} already has a great many plate readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

{{state}} already has {{readersInState}} automated license plate readers, and {{readersWithinMile}} of them sit within a mile of {{school}}. Neither number reads to me like a careful decision.

I am a student on that campus, and I would like the readers nearby taken down, with none installed to replace them. What concerns me is that a network this size grew without anyone having to justify it as a whole.

If there is a case for that scale, I would like to hear it. Otherwise I hope you will support removal. Thank you for reading.

subject: Cameras like these sit oddly beside a university
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Cameras like these sit oddly beside a university, or anywhere else people drive to work and class without expecting to be logged. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the readers around campus removed, with none added later.

My concern is the reach rather than any single camera. Reading every plate means treating every trip as potentially interesting, which is a strange footing for a city to keep with its residents.

I would be glad to know how you see it, even if you see it differently. Thank you for taking the time to read this.

subject: Is removal something you would move for
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Removal is what I am hoping for, and I would like to know whether it is something you would move for. I am a student at {{school}}, and the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are what I mean.

I would also be glad to see a decision against new installations. The cameras keep a record of people who are not accused of anything, which covers nearly everyone who uses those roads.

If the answer is no, I would still rather hear it from you. Thank you for reading.

subject: The readers near {{shortName}} could be switched off
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Switching the readers off and taking them down is what I would like to see happen around {{shortName}}. They have been reading plates belonging to people who have done nothing wrong, and I am one of those people.

I am a student at {{school}} and drive past them often. The bit that stays with me is that none of it depends on suspicion. The cameras record first and sort later, if anyone sorts at all.

Would you tell me whether you would support removal, and holding off on new ones? I would appreciate hearing it.

subject: A plain request about the plate readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Plainly, the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are something I would like removed, and I hope the city stops approving new ones. I am a student at {{school}}.

I have no expertise here and no organization behind me. What I have is a daily drive past cameras that keep a record of it, and a sense that the record is nobody's business but mine.

If you think I am wrong about that, I would rather be told than left to guess. A reply of any length would be welcome. Thank you.

subject: A second look at the readers around {{school}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Reconsidering the automated license plate readers around {{school}} is what I am hoping for, and my own view is that they should come out and that new ones should not be approved.

I am a student there. The cameras went in without much of a public conversation, as far as I can tell, and they now run on every car that passes. Ordinary trips end up in a record I cannot see.

If a second look is possible, I would like to know. If it is not, I would still like your position. Thank you.

subject: Cameras should not be the default in {{city}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Reading every plate that passes should not be the way a city watches its streets by default, or so it seems to me. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the automated license plate readers around campus removed, with no new ones installed.

A camera pointed at a specific problem is one thing. A camera pointed at everyone in case a problem appears is another, and the second is what the readers do all day.

I would be grateful to know whether you agree, and what you would be willing to support. Thank you.

subject: The readers within a mile of {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Within a mile of {{shortName}} there are {{readersWithinMile}} automated license plate readers. I would like all of them removed, and I hope none go up to take their place.

I am a student at {{school}}, so those are the roads I use daily. Each camera adds to a record of trips made by people who are not under investigation, and none of us can look at what is held or ask for it back.

Would you let me know where you stand on removal? Even a short reply would be worth having. Thank you for reading.

subject: Adding more readers to {{city}} worries me
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Adding more automated license plate readers to {{city}} is the part that worries me most, and I hope none of them are approved. I would also like the ones near {{school}} taken out.

I am a student there. Every camera makes the record more complete, and a complete record of who drove where is a thing I would rather no office had to be trusted with, however carefully it is kept.

If you see room to move on this, I would like to know. If you do not, I would still like to hear your reasoning. Thank you for reading.

subject: The readers went up without a vote
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

No vote was ever taken on whether {{city}} should read every plate on the road, at least none I can find. The automated license plate readers around {{school}} went up regardless, and I would like them removed with no new ones installed.

I am a student there, writing once. A decision this broad seems like one that should have been argued in the open, and the fact that it was not is a large part of why I am writing.

Would you tell me your position? I would be grateful for it. Thank you.

subject: A letter about the cameras, from a student
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

You will get more urgent mail than this today. Even so, I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed, and I hope no more are approved.

I am a student at {{school}}. The cameras photograph everyone who drives past, whether or not there is any reason to, and the record they keep is one I cannot see. That is what has been on my mind.

If you can spare a line to tell me where you stand, it would mean something. Thank you for reading this far.

subject: Ahead of the next plate reader renewal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Ahead of the next renewal, I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} taken out, and I hope anything that would add more is turned down.

I am a student there. What concerns me is that renewals tend to pass quietly, and a system nobody argued for at the start ends up lasting because ending it takes more effort than continuing it.

If there is a good case for renewal, I would honestly like to hear it. If there is not, I hope you will say so. Thank you for your time.

subject: The cameras at {{shortName}} bother me
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

These cameras bother me more than I expected them to. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the automated license plate readers around campus removed, with none installed afterward.

At first I did not think much about them. What changed my mind was noticing how constant they are, and that a record of my ordinary movements exists somewhere without my having agreed to it or being able to see it.

I would like to know your view, even if it is not mine. A short reply would be enough. Thank you for reading.

subject: A vote available to you this year
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

There is a vote available that would take the automated license plate readers out of the area around {{school}}, and I am hoping you will take it, along with declining anything that would add more.

I am a student there. The readers run on ordinary traffic all day, and the people in that traffic have no way to know what is kept about them. That is the part I keep returning to.

Would you tell me how you are leaning? I would rather hear a plain no than nothing at all. Thank you.

subject: Getting removal onto the agenda
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Getting removal onto the agenda would go a long way with me. The automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are what I mean, and I hope no new ones are approved either.

I am a student at {{school}}. The cameras collect from everybody who drives past, and the collecting does not stop or ask permission. I would rather the city did without them entirely.

If putting this forward is not something you can do, I would still like to know your own position on it. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: How many readers does {{city}} actually need
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

How many automated license plate readers does {{city}} actually need? My own answer is none, and I would start with the ones around {{school}}, where I am a student.

I would like those removed and no new ones installed. The cameras work on everyone who passes, which means the great majority of what they collect is about people going to class or to work. Keeping that seems like the wrong instinct for a city.

If your answer differs from mine, I would like to hear it in your words. Thank you for the time.

subject: Hoping for not one more camera
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Not one more camera is what I am hoping for, and I would like the automated license plate readers already around {{school}} removed too, since leaving those while refusing new ones only freezes the problem where it is.

I am a student there. Being recorded by default on the drive to class is what I object to, and no policy about how the records get used changes the fact that they exist.

Would you tell me whether removal is something you could back? I would be grateful for a reply.

subject: Your office could settle this quickly
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Your office could settle this quickly, and I hope it will. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed, and the next request for more declined.

I am a student at {{school}}, so I pass those cameras several times a week. The record they build is about people who have not been accused of anything, and it stays long after whatever prompted the collection has passed.

If you would tell me where you stand, I would appreciate it. Even a sentence would be better than wondering. Thank you for reading.

subject: Keeping this short about the campus readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Keeping this short seems fairest to both of us. The automated license plate readers near {{school}} are ones I would like removed, and I hope no new ones go in. I am a student there.

The cameras read every plate, all the time, including mine. What I cannot get past is that the record of an ordinary drive is kept by default, with no way for me to see it or ask about it.

A short answer with your position would be welcome, whatever it says. Thank you for reading.

subject: This is my only letter about the cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

This is my only letter about this, so I will be direct rather than long. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed, and I hope the city stops installing them.

I am a student at {{school}}. The readers watch a road rather than a person, which sounds harmless until you notice that everyone using the road is being recorded and none of us were asked.

If you would send back a line saying where you stand, I would be grateful. Thank you for taking the time.

subject: A look at what sits around {{school}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Looking at what sits around {{school}}, I find automated license plate readers running constantly and reading the plate of every car that passes. I would like them removed, and I hope no more are approved.

I am a student there. None of this was put to the people who drive those roads daily, and the record it produces is not one any of us can see. Both of those bother me.

Would you tell me whether removal is something you would support? A brief reply would be plenty. Thank you.

subject: The number of readers near {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Somewhere in the streets around {{shortName}} sit {{readersWithinMile}} automated license plate readers. I would like all of them taken out, and I hope nothing replaces them.

I am a student at {{school}}. The figure surprised me, but what stayed with me afterward was how ordinary the traffic they read is. Almost none of it has anything to do with a crime, and all of it gets recorded anyway.

I would be glad to hear your position, even in a sentence. If there is context I am missing, I would like that too. Thank you.

subject: Hoping for a no on new plate readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A no vote on new automated license plate readers is what I am hoping for, along with removal of the ones already around {{school}}. Being a student there is my only reason for writing.

The cameras record everybody who drives past, and the people recorded have no way to check what is held or how long it lasts. That imbalance is the part which concerns me most.

If you would let me know where you stand, I would appreciate it. Thank you for reading a letter from one student who lives with these daily.

subject: An ordinary complaint about the surveillance cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

This is an ordinary complaint from an ordinary resident. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed, and I hope the city will not install more.

I am a student at {{school}}, in {{city}} for most of the year. My worry is not dramatic. Cameras that log every car build a record of people who are not suspected of anything, and that record sits somewhere out of reach of the people in it.

Would you write back with your view? I would be grateful for it, whichever way it goes. Thank you.

subject: Taking the readers off the poles near campus
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Taking the readers off the poles is what I would like to see around {{school}}. They have been reading plates from every car in the area, mine included, and I hope no new ones are installed either.

I am a student here. The cameras never pause and never forget, and the people they record are almost entirely people going about a normal day. That combination is what I find hard to sit with.

I would value knowing your position, even briefly. If you see it differently, I would still like to hear why. Thank you.

subject: The readers have quietly become permanent
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Whatever the readers were meant to be at the start, they have become permanent, and I would like them removed from the area around {{school}}. I hope no new ones are installed in their place.

I am a student there. Permanence is the part that worries me. A tool brought in for a particular problem stays long after, and the record it keeps grows with it, covering people who never had anything to do with the problem.

Would you tell me whether you would support removal? I would be grateful for an answer. Thank you.

subject: The readers cover the roads I use daily
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The roads I use to get to class are covered by these cameras, and I would rather they were not. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed, with none installed later.

There is no way to avoid them short of not driving. That is what makes this different from a camera I could choose to walk past or not, and it is why I am writing rather than shrugging.

Would you share your position with me? Thank you for reading.

subject: Reading everyone's plate to find one
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Reading everyone's plate in order to find one person's seems like a poor trade to me, and I would like {{city}} to stop making it. The automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are ones I hope will come down, with no new ones installed.

I am a student at {{school}}. The people whose plates get read are mostly students, workers, and residents doing nothing of interest to anyone.

If you weigh that trade differently, I would like to understand why. A reply of any length would be welcome. Thank you.

subject: Old readers out, new ones not approved
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Old ones out, new ones not approved. That is what I am hoping for with the automated license plate cameras around {{shortName}}, and I am writing as a student at {{school}}.

Half a solution would not settle it for me. Removing the readers while leaving the door open to replacements, or refusing new ones while the current cameras keep running, would leave the same record being built either way.

I would be grateful to know whether both halves are something you could support, and if only one of them is possible, which one that would be. Thank you for reading.

subject: Writing only for myself about the campus readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Speaking only for myself, I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope no new ones are installed. I am a student there and represent nobody but me.

The cameras collect constantly from people who have done nothing to invite it. Whatever protections exist around the records, the collecting itself is the thing I object to, and it happens before any of those protections matter.

If you would tell me your view, I would appreciate it. Thank you for taking a moment with this.

subject: About the next camera proposal to reach you
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The next camera proposal to reach your desk is one I hope you will decline, and I would also like the automated license plate readers already installed around {{shortName}} taken out.

I am a student at {{school}}. What worries me is the direction rather than any single approval. Each new camera makes the record of ordinary movement more complete, and nothing about that process invites a decision to stop.

I would be glad to hear where you stand. Even a short note would be worth having. Thank you for reading.

subject: A camera on a pole does not know me
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A camera on a pole does not know who I am, and I would rather it did not find out. The automated license plate readers around {{school}} are ones I would like removed, with none installed to replace them.

I am a student there. Being read and recorded on a drive to class is not something I agreed to, and no one asked. The record outlasts the trip by a very long way.

If there is a reason to keep them that I have not understood, I would like to hear it. Thank you.

subject: Most people never notice the readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Most people in {{city}} could not say how many cameras read their plate on the way to work, and that is part of why this is easy to leave alone. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the readers around campus removed, with no new ones approved.

Not noticing something is different from agreeing to it. The record builds either way, about people who have done nothing to prompt it.

Would you tell me where you stand? I would be grateful for a reply, however brief. Thank you.

subject: Quietly installed and quietly running
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Quietly installed cameras that quietly keep running are how a city ends up watching everyone without ever deciding to. The automated license plate readers around {{school}} strike me that way, and I would like them removed with none added later.

I am a student there. My concern is with how little deliberation a system like this needs in order to persist, compared with how much it would take to end.

If you see this differently, I would genuinely like to know why. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: The plate reader program in {{city}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The plate reader program in {{city}} is one I would like to see ended, with the automated readers around {{school}} removed first, and I hope anything that would add more is turned down.

I am a student on that campus. The cameras keep a record of people who are not suspected of anything, and there is no point at which any of us agreed to be part of it.

Would you tell me whether ending it is something you could support? I would be grateful for an answer either way. Thank you.

subject: One student with one request
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

One student with one request: I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} taken out of the area, and I hope no new ones are approved.

I am at {{school}} and writing on my own. Cameras that read every plate make a record of ordinary trips, and the people in those trips are not consulted and cannot see what is kept. That is the whole of my worry, stated once.

If you would send back your position, even a line or two, I would appreciate it. Thank you for reading a letter that asks for nothing else.

subject: No public conversation came before the cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

There was no public conversation before these cameras went up, at least none I have been able to find. The automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are ones I would like removed, with no new ones installed.

I am a student at {{school}}. A decision that puts every driver into a record seems like one that should have been argued in the open, and I would like the chance to see that argument even now.

Would you tell me your view? I would be grateful for it. Thank you for reading.

subject: My answer on the plate readers is no
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

My answer on the automated license plate readers is no. I would like the ones around {{shortName}} removed, and I hope any proposal to add more is turned down.

I am a student at {{school}}, and this is the only letter I plan to send about it. The cameras record everyone who drives past, which is a great many people to gather information about in order to find the rare one worth finding.

If you would let me know where you stand, I would appreciate hearing it. Thank you.

subject: Removal is the outcome I am hoping for
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Nothing short of removal would settle this for me. A review or a policy update would still leave the automated license plate readers around {{school}} reading plates, and I would like them out, with none installed afterward.

I am a student there. My worry is with the collecting itself. Rules about how records get used matter, but they apply to a record that should not have been made about people who did nothing.

If you see a middle path I am missing, I would like to hear it. Thank you for reading.

subject: Every approach to {{shortName}} has a camera
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Driving toward {{shortName}} means passing automated license plate readers, and I would rather it did not. I would like the cameras removed, and I hope the city stops installing them.

I am a student at {{school}}, so I make that drive constantly. Each time, a record is made of a trip that has nothing to do with anyone's investigation, and that record does not belong to me even though it is about me.

Would you tell me whether you would support removal? A short reply would be welcome. Thank you.

subject: Acting on the readers before the term ends
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Acting on this would not take much, as best I can tell. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope the next set is refused.

I am a student there. The cameras are already installed and already running, which makes doing nothing the easy option. That is exactly why I thought it was worth writing to ask.

If there is a step in this that is harder than it looks from outside, I would like to understand it. Thank you for your time.

subject: The simplest version of what I want
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The simplest version of what I want is cameras out and no new cameras in, starting with the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}.

I am a student at {{school}}, which is the only standing I have here. What bothers me is that a record of every trip made by every driver exists without anyone in the car having agreed to it, and without any way to look at it.

I would be grateful for a reply telling me your position. If it differs from mine, I would still like to hear it. Thank you.

subject: Do you support removing the campus readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Do you support removing the automated license plate readers around {{school}}? That is really my only question, and I ask it as a student there who would also like new installations ruled out.

The cameras read every plate that passes, mine among them, and keep what they read. I have not found anything that explains why that is necessary on roads used mostly by people going to class and work.

An answer either way would help me more than silence. Thank you for taking the time to read this.

subject: A ring of cameras around a university
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A ring of cameras around a university was somebody's idea, and it is not one I can make sense of. The automated license plate readers near {{school}} are ones I would like removed, and I hope no new ones are approved.

I am a student here. Campuses are full of people who have just arrived in a city and have no particular reason to be logged coming and going. That is a strange place to start collecting.

Would you let me know your position? I would be grateful for it. Thank you.

subject: A position on the campus cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Having a position on this from you would help me, if you have not already stated one. Mine is that the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} should be removed and that the city should stop adding them.

I am a student at {{school}}. The cameras collect from everyone, continuously, and the people collected from have no way to see or question the record.

If your view is different, I would rather hear it plainly than not hear it. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: Removal of the readers around {{school}} this year
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

This year would be a good one to remove the automated license plate readers around {{school}}, and to decide against new installations. That is what I am hoping for.

I am a student there. The readers run every day on traffic that is almost entirely ordinary, and the record they build is kept out of sight of the people it describes. Time only makes that record longer.

Would you tell me whether removal is something you would support this year? I would be grateful for an answer. Thank you for reading.

subject: The readers do not belong in {{city}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Cameras that read plates automatically do not belong in {{city}}, to my mind, and least of all ringing a campus. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the readers near campus removed, with no new ones installed.

What worries me is that the collecting is indiscriminate by design. It cannot be otherwise, since a camera has no way of knowing which car matters until after it has recorded them all.

If there is an answer to that I have not considered, I would like to hear it. Thank you.

subject: A single decision would settle this
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A single decision would settle this for me: the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} taken out, and new ones ruled out at the same time.

I am a student at {{school}}, writing once and for myself. The cameras photograph every car, mine included, and the record goes to a place I have no access to. Nobody asked whether that was an acceptable arrangement.

I would be glad to know your view, even if it is not the one I am hoping for. A short reply would be more than I have now. Thank you for reading.

subject: An objection from one constituent
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

This is an objection from a constituent, filed once and meant seriously. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and no new ones installed.

I am a student there and in {{city}} most of the year. My concern is that a record of ordinary movement is being built continuously about people who have not been accused of anything, and none of us can see it.

If you would tell me where you stand, I would appreciate it. Even a brief reply would be worth having. Thank you.

subject: What happens to the plates the cameras collect
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

What happens to a plate after a camera reads it is something I have not been able to find a trustworthy answer to, and that is one reason I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed.

I am a student at {{school}}, and I hope no new ones are installed either. Not knowing where a record of my movements goes is uncomfortable in a way I did not expect.

If you know the answer, I would like to hear it. If not, I hope you will consider removal. Thank you.

subject: Almost everyone recorded has done nothing
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Almost everyone those cameras record has done nothing, and that includes me. I am a student at {{school}}, and I would like the automated license plate readers around campus removed, with none installed later.

The ratio is what unsettles me. A tool aimed at the rare case ends up holding information about everybody else, and everybody else never comes into it except as data that happened to be nearby.

I would be grateful to know your view on removal, even in a line or two. Thank you for reading.

subject: A request from someone who lives here
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

From someone who lives in the area most of the year: I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope the next request for more is refused.

I am a student there, so my time in {{city}} is real if not permanent. The cameras log my car on trips that concern nobody, and that log stays after I have forgotten the trip entirely.

Would you tell me whether you would back removal? A short answer would be plenty. Thank you for reading this.

subject: An end to the readers around {{shortName}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

An end to the readers is what would suit me: no automated license plate readers around {{shortName}}, and none installed afterward to make up the difference.

I am a student at {{school}}. My worry is simple enough. Cameras that record every car build a history of people who have done nothing, and that history sits somewhere none of us can reach or review.

If you would let me know whether you could support removal, I would be grateful. Thank you for reading a letter from one student who passes them daily.

subject: Cameras around campus, from a student
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Writing as a student at {{school}}, I would like the automated license plate readers around campus removed, and I hope no new ones are installed. That is the whole request.

The cameras sit on roads I use every day. What sits badly is that a record of ordinary trips is made automatically, kept indefinitely, and shown to nobody who is in it. I would rather my city did without that.

If you would reply with your position, I would appreciate it, whichever way it falls. Thank you for reading.

subject: Stopping before the next installation goes in
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Stopping before the next installation would be a start, and working backward from there would be better. The automated license plate readers already around {{school}} are ones I would like removed as well.

I am a student there. Every additional camera makes the record more complete, and completeness is the thing I find hard about this. Nobody set out to build a history of where residents drive, but that is what accumulates.

Would you tell me where you stand? I would be grateful for a reply. Thank you.

subject: A brief note about the plate readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Briefly, the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are ones I would like removed, and I hope {{city}} stops approving new ones. I am a student at {{school}}.

I write on behalf of no group and have no expertise to offer. I drive past these cameras constantly, and the thought that each pass is recorded and kept somewhere I cannot see has been bothering me for a while.

Your position would be worth knowing, whatever it is. Would you write back and tell me whether you could support removal and refuse new installations? Thank you for the time.

subject: The answer I am hoping for is removal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The answer I am hoping for is removal, followed by a decision not to install more. I am a student at {{school}}, and the automated license plate readers around campus are what I mean.

Reviews and policy updates would leave the cameras in place and running. What concerns me is the record itself, made about people who have given no reason for it and kept beyond any reason for keeping it.

If you would tell me whether removal is possible, I would be grateful. Thank you for reading.

subject: Bringing removal to a vote
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Bringing removal to a vote is something I hope you will consider. The automated license plate readers around {{school}} should come down, in my view, and no new ones approved after that.

I am a student there. The cameras record every car that passes, mine included, and the people recorded have no say in it and no sight of what is held. A vote would at least put that decision in the open.

Would you let me know whether you would support one, and how you would vote if it came about? Thank you for reading this.

subject: The easiest thing would be to leave this alone
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

The easiest thing to do with this is nothing, which is why I thought it was worth writing. I would like the automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} removed, and no new ones installed.

I am a student at {{school}}. Programs like this continue on their own momentum, and the record they keep grows quietly, covering people who never came into anyone's inquiry.

If you would tell me your position, I would be grateful. Even a sentence would be more than I have now. Thank you for reading.

subject: Both halves of this request matter to me
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Both halves of this matter to me: removal of the automated license plate readers around {{school}}, and a decision against the next batch. I am a student there.

Doing only one would leave the same thing happening at a different pace. The cameras collect from everyone who drives past, and the record they build is about people who have not been accused of anything.

I would be grateful to know whether both are things you could support. If only one is, I would like to hear which. Thank you for reading.

subject: The cameras will outlast my time at {{school}}
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

These readers will outlast my time at {{school}} unless somebody decides otherwise, and I am hoping you might be that somebody. I would like them removed, and new proposals turned down.

I am a student here for a few years, and the record the cameras keep will be here longer than I am. That gap between how long the collecting lasts and how long anyone remembers the reason for it is what worries me.

Would you tell me your view? I would be grateful for it. Thank you.

subject: A no from one constituent
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

My own view is no. The automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} are ones I would like removed, and I hope the city approves no more of them.

I am a student at {{school}} and one constituent with one opinion. The cameras read every plate that passes and keep the result, and nobody in those cars was asked whether that was acceptable. It does not seem acceptable to me.

If you would send back a line with your position, I would be grateful for it. Thank you for reading.

subject: Another look at the plate reader program
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Another look at this would be worth the time, I think. The automated license plate readers around {{school}} are ones I would like removed, and I hope new ones are refused.

I am a student there. When the readers went in, they may have looked like a small addition. What they amount to now is a steady record of ordinary movement by people who have done nothing, and that is worth reconsidering.

Would you tell me whether you would support removal? I would appreciate an answer. Thank you.

subject: Asking directly rather than signing a petition
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Rather than sign a petition, I thought I would ask you directly: would you support removing the automated license plate readers around {{school}}, and refusing new ones?

I am a student there, writing once and for myself. The cameras photograph everyone who drives past and keep the record out of reach of the people in it. That is what I would like to see end.

If your answer is no, I would still like to know, and to hear the reasoning behind it. A short note would be plenty, and I would not write again. Thank you for reading.

subject: Ahead of any vote on the readers
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Ahead of any vote on this, I would like to know your position, and I will offer mine first. The automated license plate readers around {{shortName}} should come out, and no new ones should go in.

I am a student at {{school}}. What concerns me is that these cameras record constantly and indiscriminately, and the people recorded have no way to see, question, or remove what is held.

Would you write back with where you stand? Even a short answer would help me more than guessing does. Thank you for reading a letter from one student.

subject: The last thing I will say about the cameras
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Once, and then I will leave it alone: I would like the automated license plate readers around {{school}} removed, and I hope the city installs no more of them.

I am a student there. The cameras record ordinary trips made by people who are not under suspicion, and the record lasts far longer than the trip or the reason for it. That is what I have been turning over.

If you would tell me where you stand, I would be grateful. Thank you for reading this one letter.

subject: Asking whether you would put removal on an agenda
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

There are {{readersWithinMile}} automated plate readers within a mile of {{school}}, and what unsettles me is that none of them arrived because students asked for them. As a student here I have no way to change that on my own. The first step is procedural rather than dramatic, since somebody has to put the question on an agenda.

I am asking you to be that person, and I would like to know whether you will. The item would read plainly: remove the readers already installed around campus and authorize no new ones.

A retention rule would leave the network standing, and so would an annual report. What would change conditions on the ground is taking equipment down and declining to add more.

Would you sponsor that item? If something makes it difficult, I would genuinely like to understand what.

subject: Asking for a yes or no on removal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

One line would answer this, which is why I am asking rather than arguing.

Would you vote to remove the automated plate readers around {{school}} and to bar new installations in {{city}}? A yes or a no is enough for me. Should the answer be yes, I would like to know when such a vote could be scheduled. If it is no, I would like the reason, so that I can repeat it accurately to other students rather than guessing at it.

What troubles me is that the cameras went up without a public decision by the people they record. Reversing that needs a public decision too, and that part is not something a student can do.

A one word reply would count as a complete answer, and I would be grateful for it.

subject: Letting the plate reader contract lapse at renewal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Every surveillance contract has an end date, and that date looks to me like the least painful place to undo a decision. No lawsuit would be needed and no buyout would have to be negotiated. The {{role}} lets the agreement lapse and directs that the equipment come down.

That is what I am asking for with the automated plate readers near {{school}}. At the next renewal, I hope you will vote no, and I hope the same motion will make clear that no replacement system is to be installed. A lapsed contract with a new vendor waiting would not feel like a change to me.

I am one student writing one letter, and I never agreed to be logged on my way to campus.
