subject: Government functions should not run on subscriptions
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Subscriptions are relationships of continuing dependence. Applied to email or accounting software, that is fine. For a system recording where residents drive, it puts a recurring invoice between the public and a public function.

Stop paying and the capability disappears, along with, possibly, the records. Keep paying and the terms are whatever the holder of the platform says they are at renewal.

Neither branch looks like a good place for {{city}} to stand, and that is what prompted me to write. I hope you will support removing the plate readers around {{shortName}} and installing no new ones. Would you tell me which of those branches you believe {{city}} is on today? I am a student here, and I would be grateful for your reading of it.

subject: Independent reporting before any renewal is considered
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Renewal decisions are the only real leverage a council has, and they come around rarely. Before the next one for the plate readers around {{shortName}}, I would ask you to seek something simple, which is a report about this system produced by someone other than the company selling it.

Without that, the council votes on the seller's account of the seller's product. Few people would accept the same arrangement in an audit of city finances, and the stakes here are not lower.

My actual preference is removal. Take the readers near campus out, and add none. If you will not go that far, would you at least commit publicly to independent reporting before any renewal? I am a student here, and I would be grateful either way.

subject: Questions I have not been able to answer
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Here is what I have been unable to work out about the plate readers near {{shortName}}. Who holds the records, and on whose hardware? Can {{city}} inspect the system without the company's cooperation? Does public records law reach the copy the company keeps?

Each of those has an answer. None of them is available to a student willing to spend an afternoon looking, which tells me something about how the program was set up.

My request does not depend on the answers. Remove the plate readers around campus, and install no new ones. If you would rather resolve the questions first, would you put them to staff and share what comes back? I would be grateful for that, and I thank you for reading.

subject: A request for custody answers only you can get
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Staff answer questions from people in your position that they will not answer from mine, and that asymmetry is the reason for this note.

The plate readers around {{shortName}} run on infrastructure held by a private company. What I would like established on the record is who holds the data and whether {{city}} can audit the system without the company's help.

My own position is that the cameras should be removed from around campus and that none should replace them, which would make those questions academic. Would you ask them anyway, and tell me what you learn? I am one student writing on my own behalf, with no organization behind me, and I would be grateful for whatever you are able to find out.

subject: Who holds the keys to this system
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A short question, since your staff are busy. For the plate readers near {{shortName}}, who can switch the system off, and who can read the whole database?

If either answer is a private company, then {{city}} hosts a surveillance program it does not command. That seems worth knowing before the next budget cycle, and worth explaining to the people being recorded, a student like me among them.

I would like the readers around campus removed and no new ones installed, which is the cleanest answer to all of it. Would you tell me where you stand, and what you find out? Even a brief note would be more than I have managed to gather on my own, and I would appreciate it.

subject: Depending on a service a company can withdraw
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Any hosted service can stop working, and the customer's remedy is contractual rather than practical. A police department that has built routine work around a plate reader platform is exposed to a business decision it does not control.

That exposure reads to me as an argument against depending on the system at all. A capability that can be withdrawn was never really a public capability.

So I am asking that {{city}} stop relying on it around {{shortName}}, removing the readers near campus and installing no new ones. Should you disagree, would you tell me what contingency {{city}} has if the platform became unavailable, and who judged that acceptable? I am a student here, and I would be grateful for your thinking on it.

subject: A demonstration is not the same as deliberation
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Sales presentations are persuasive by design. A demonstration shows a system finding the car you wanted found, and it never shows the archive of everyone else, because that part makes a poor demo.

Decisions about surveillance taken shortly after a demonstration tend to reflect the demonstration. The questions that matter, about custody and about what happens at the end, do not fit in the room.

Around {{shortName}}, {{readersWithinMile}} readers within a mile are the result, and I am a student living inside that mile. I hope you will support removing them and installing no new ones. Would you tell me what deliberation, if any, {{city}} held that was not shaped by the seller? I would be glad to be told there was more than I can find.

subject: Recording people who are here only a few years
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Many of us around {{school}} are here for a short stretch of our lives. Our movements are recorded on the same terms as anyone else's and stored by a company with no obligation to us at all.

That combination is worth naming gently. A population with little political voice is entered into a private database, and the people in it have almost no way to ask the holder anything. As a student, that is the part I find genuinely worrying, and I raise it as a request to look again rather than as a grievance.

I hope you will support removing the plate readers around campus and installing none in future. Would you tell me whether the position of the campus population figured into this at all?

subject: How a tool quietly became infrastructure
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A tool gets picked up and put down. Infrastructure runs continuously and shapes what everything around it assumes. Plate readers near {{shortName}} were probably sold as the first sort of thing and have become the second, with a private company as the operator.

Infrastructure decisions deserve a level of deliberation this one does not appear to have had, including public hearings and a documented way to reverse course. I have looked for signs of either and come up short.

What I am asking is that {{city}} treat removal as the correction, taking the readers near campus out and authorizing none to replace them. Would you tell me whether you consider this program infrastructure, and whether it has ever been reviewed as such? I am a student here and would value your view.

subject: Terms that will bind councils not yet elected
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A long commitment made today constrains the people who will hold your seat later. That is normal for a building and questionable for a surveillance capability, because the political judgment behind it may not survive the term of the agreement.

Future members will inherit the cameras around {{shortName}} along with a relationship the company has every reason to continue. Their room to reconsider will be narrower than yours is now, and that narrowing is what concerns me.

The kindest thing to do for them may be to close it out. I hope you will support removing the plate readers near campus and approving no new ones. Would you tell me how long the current commitment runs and what ending it would require? I am a student here and would be grateful to know.

subject: A written answer on custody before any renewal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Nothing in this note requires you to agree with me about surveillance. It asks only that {{city}} be able to say, in writing, who holds the plate data collected around {{shortName}} and under what conditions anyone else can reach it.

If that answer exists, publishing it costs nothing. Should it not exist, then a program running near {{school}} has been operating without anyone establishing the most basic fact about it, and that possibility is what worries me most.

For my part, I would like the readers around campus removed and no new ones installed. Would you seek a written custody answer before any renewal, and would you share it with the student who asked? I would be grateful, whatever the answer turns out to be.

subject: What a genuine audit of this system would need
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

An audit worth the name would need access to raw logs rather than company summaries, and a reviewer the company cannot turn away. Anything less produces a document that reassures without verifying.

My guess is that {{city}} has neither, for the plate readers around {{shortName}} or for anything else on that platform. I would be pleased to be wrong, and I would much rather hear it from you than from a marketing page.

The simpler path is still removal, taking the cameras near campus out of service and installing none in their place. Would you tell me whether {{city}} holds the access a genuine audit would require? I am a student here, and I have asked around without getting close to an answer.

subject: A public decision that ended up inside a contract
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Strip this issue down and one thing is left. A decision about how closely people in {{city}} are watched now lives inside a commercial arrangement, where the public can neither read the terms nor reach the records.

Everything else follows from that. Whatever the merits of the technology, a function this consequential should not rest with a party answering to customers rather than to residents of {{state}}.

My request is the one I would make to any member of {{role}}, which is to remove the plate readers around {{shortName}} and install no new ones. Would you tell me your position, and whether you will raise the question of custody before the next vote? I am a student here, and I would be grateful for a reply of any length.
